content: The base of the lung is wide and concave in shape. It rests on the convex surface of the diaphragm, which serves as a separation between the right lung and the right lobe of the liver, as well as between the left lung and the left lobe of the liver, the stomach, and the spleen. Due to the diaphragm being positioned higher on the right side compared to the left, the concavity of the base of the right lung is more pronounced than that of the left lung. On the lateral and posterior sides, the base of the lung is bordered by a thin, sharp edge. This margin extends into the phrenicocostal sinus of the pleura, which is located between the lower ribs and the costal attachment of the diaphragm. During the process of inspiration, the base of the lung moves downward, while during expiration, it moves upward.
